concepts.title: Poetry as Making: The Origin of the Word
concepts.definition: The word poetry originates from a Greek word meaning 'to make'. A poet is thus a maker, and a poem something made -- language crafted, not merely used. This framing places emphasis on the poem as an artefact of deliberate artistry.
concepts.key_idea: A poem is a made thing -- the etymology itself teaches that poetry is craft before it is confession.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww111.txt introduction (greek origin meaning to make, poet as maker, poem as something made)
question_patterns: from which greek word does poetry originate and what does it mean
in class 11 poetry introduction: why is a poet called a maker
what does the etymology of poetry suggest about reading poems
distinguish making a poem from merely expressing feelings
why is a poem compared to a crafted artefact
explain the idea that a poem is something that is made

solution_steps.explain: The Greek root meaning 'to make' underlies both poetry and poet.
Making implies choice of words, shape and sound -- a poem is built, not poured out.
Readers should attend to craft -- how the poem is made -- as much as to what it says.

concepts.title: How a Poem Communicates: Compression, Music and Suggestion
concepts.definition: Unlike prose, a poem communicates through compression -- maximum meaning in minimum words -- through the music of rhythm and sound, and through suggestion, where images carry meanings that statement cannot. Reading poetry asks for attention to these, not just extraction of a paraphrase.
concepts.key_idea: Say more with less, sing while saying -- a poem works by compression, music and suggestion together.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww111.txt reading sections (compression of language, rhythm and sound patterns, imagery and suggestion, how to read a poem)
question_patterns: how does a poem compress meaning into few words
in class 11 poetry introduction: what role does sound and rhythm play in a poem
explain suggestion and imagery as poetic devices
why should a poem not be reduced to a prose paraphrase
how is reading poetry different from reading prose
give an example of a line where sound reinforces meaning

solution_steps.explain: Each word in a poem carries weight -- there is no filler in good verse.
Rhythm, rhyme and repetition organise the poem for ear and memory.
Images and associations carry surplus meaning that paraphrase would destroy.

concepts.title: The Poems of This Section: A Preview
concepts.definition: The introduction previews the anthology's range: sonnets and odes, lyrics and narrative verse, poets from Shakespeare and Wordsworth to modern voices -- poems of love, nature, alienation, language and loss -- each chosen to display poetry's variety of form and feeling.
concepts.key_idea: A doorway to an anthology -- forms from sonnet to free verse, feelings from love to exile.
concepts.textbook_ref: keww111.txt preview sections (range of poems in the anthology, shakespeare wordsworth keats auden hughes, variety of themes and forms)
question_patterns: name the poets and poems included in the poetry section
in class 11 poetry introduction: what variety of themes does the anthology cover
distinguish a sonnet from an ode as forms mentioned

how does the section balance old and modern poets
what unites such different poems in one anthology

solution_steps.explain: From Shakespeare and Wordsworth to Auden and modern Indian poets, the range spans centuries and cultures.
Love, nature, war, exile, language and everyday family life all find their poems.
The variety is deliberate -- an anthology training readers in poetry's many shapes.

worked_examples.question_pattern: A friend says poems are just overflowing emotions. Use the 'making' etymology to answer.

solution_template.explain: Feeling often starts a poem -- but feeling alone is not a poem.
Poetry means making: emotion must be given form -- words ordered, sound shaped.
The poet is a maker first; the emotion arrives to us already crafted.

worked_examples.question_pattern: Why does the introduction warn against reducing a poem to a prose paraphrase?

solution_template.explain: A paraphrase preserves the statement or content of the poem.
It loses rhythm, sound patterning, image and suggestion -- half the poem's meaning.
Reading poetry means experiencing the made thing whole, not extracting a summary.
